task.title: Borders and rounded corners
task.shortdesc: A border is a line around the padding of a box. Each side has a style, a width and a color, and the corners can be rounded.

info.p: The border property sets the width, the style and the color of the four borders. Write the three values in any order:
The style is the value that turns a border on. The initial style is none, and a border with that style has no width, whatever width you set. If a border does not show, check that it has a style.
The border-style property takes one to four of these values:

ul.li: dashed is a line of dashes, and dotted a line of round dots.
double is two lines with a space between them. The lines and the space are a third of the width each.
groove and ridge are two lines of a lighter and a darker shade of the color. A groove looks cut into the page and a ridge looks raised.
inset and outset are one line, darker on the top and the left for an inset, and on the bottom and the right for an outset.

image.alt: Eight rectangles, each with a border of a different style: solid, dashed, dotted, double, groove, ridge, inset and outset.

info.p: With two to four values, the sides take them as in margin: one value sets all sides, two values set top and bottom, then left and right, and so on.
This note has a border at the top and at the bottom only.

The border-width property takes one to four widths. A width is a length that is not negative, or one of three keywords: thin is 1px, medium is 3px and thick is 5px. A pixel is 0.75pt. The initial width is medium.
The border-color property takes one to four colors. Its initial value is currentcolor, which is the color of the text of the element, so a border that has no color is drawn in the color of the text.
Where two sides of different colors meet, the change of color is on the diagonal from the outer corner to the inner corner.

Each side has properties of its own. The physical sides are top, right, bottom and left, and the logical sides, which follow the direction of the text, are block-start, block-end, inline-start and inline-end. For each side there are four properties:

ul.li: border-side sets the width, the style and the color, like border.
border-side-width, border-side-style and border-side-color set one part.

info.p: The properties border-block and border-inline set the two sides of an axis. They also have the three parts, such as border-inline-width, which takes one or two values.
This heading has a thin line under it in horizontal text, and a line at the end of the block axis in any other writing mode.

The border-radius property sets the radius of the four corners. A radius is a length or a percentage that is not negative. A percentage is a part of the width of the box for the horizontal radius and of its height for the vertical one. The values are read like those of margin: one value sets all corners, and with more values the first is the top left corner and the rest follow clockwise.
A corner can be an ellipse. Write the horizontal radii, a slash and the vertical radii. border-radius: 12pt / 6pt gives each corner a horizontal radius of 12pt and a vertical radius of 6pt.

fig.title: A circular and an elliptical corner

image.alt: Two rounded rectangles. The first has corners that follow a dashed circle, and the second has corners that follow a dashed ellipse.

info.p: To set one corner, use border-top-left-radius, border-top-right-radius, border-bottom-right-radius or border-bottom-left-radius. They take one value for a circle or two for an ellipse. The properties border-start-start-radius, border-start-end-radius, border-end-start-radius and border-end-end-radius name the corners by the direction of the text. The properties border-top-radius, border-right-radius, border-bottom-radius, border-left-radius, border-block-start-radius, border-block-end-radius, border-inline-start-radius and border-inline-end-radius set the two corners of one side.
The corner property and the properties corner-top-left, corner-top and the like set the radius of a corner or of a side too.

The rounded corner clips the background of the box, and the border follows the curve. If the radii of a side are larger than the side, CSSMedia makes all the radii of the box smaller in the same proportion, until they fit. The inner edge of a border has a radius that is the outer radius less the width of the border.
